column1: #Text=So the proud lady of Mortain looked down upon Beltane in amaze, for
#Text= there was none in all the Duchy, knight, noble or princeling, who dared
#Text= gainsay her lightest word; wherefore, I say, she stared upon this bold
#Text= forest knave with his golden hair and gentle eyes, his curved lips and
#Text= square chin; and in eyes and mouth and chin was a look of
#Text= masterfulness, challenging, commanding.
#Text=And, meeting that look, her
#Text= heart leapt most strangely with sudden, sweet thrill, so that she
#Text= lowered her gaze lest he should see, and when she spake her voice was
#Text= low and very sweet:
#Text=
#Text= "Tell me I pray, why seek you my name, and wherefore?"
#Text=Quoth Beltane, soft and slow as one that dreams:
#Text=
#Text= "I have seen thine eyes look at me from the flowers, ere now, have
#Text= heard thy laughter in the brook, and found thy beauty in all fair
#Text= things: methinks thy name should be a most sweet name."
